content.text: {"narrative":[{"claim":"India faced a medium-severity, open risk that fragmented definitions, reporting formats and data systems had made it difficult to measure progress consistently and spotlight inequalities.","cites":["risk:2"]},{"claim":"The Government of India launched the Swachh Bharat (Clean India) Mission in 2014, and 110 million toilets were constructed under it.","cites":["fact:01a126b0-eae7-7093-95d5-28fef2b994be","kpi:19"]},{"claim":"India reached 580 million people with improved drinking water and 550 million people with basic sanitation over the last 10 years.","cites":["kpi:16","kpi:15"]},{"claim":"In 2024, 59.3 million people in India accessed safely managed water and 17.9 million accessed safely managed sanitation.","cites":["kpi:23","kpi:22"]},{"claim":"Improved access to clean water and sanitation played a pivotal role by dramatically reducing incidence of diarrhoeal disease, malnutrition and infection.","cites":["fact:01a126b0-eaeb-7085-93ba-272b9b509583"]},{"claim":"The Government of India invested over $120 billion in water and sanitation.","cites":["kpi:18"]}]}
